title: Father Boyle Stevenson and the country brass band
summary: His father played cornet in a plantation brass band with relatives, taught by Professor Jim Humphrey; his father died around the First World War when Burke was about 15.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did your father and mother play any music?
My father was a trumpet player. In that time, they used cornets, short horns. Yes, sir.
Had he played in any band up there?
Yeah, he was in the brass band. Him, a fellow by the name of Ellick Taylor, Ben Cole, and my uncle William Stevenson. My daddy was named Boyle Stevenson.
How old was he? Do you remember about when he was born?
No, I couldn't remember. How old he was when he died? When he died, he was around about 40, 44 years old when he died.
When did he die? Do you remember about?
He died in the year of the First World War.
So you were about 14 or 15 years old, something like that?
Was that a band that Charlie Love, that Charlie Love, his father played too, didn't he? No, that wasn't a band Charlie Love.

No, that wasn't a band Charlie Love. No, that wasn't a band Charlie Love. Well, this band, my father played in, they had a professor by the name of Jim Humphrey, used to teach him. Oh, yeah, I've heard of that. As well as Humphrey, a grandfather. Yeah. He used to come out there in the country, that we used in the country at the time, a place by the name of Dair Range, Dair Range Plantation.
Well, that was down for Jim Robinson and Sonny Henry.
